newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market down 70 bps to 10.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market down 70 bps to 10.9 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate slipped to 10.9 percent on Friday from 11.6 percent amid a short supply of kuna funds.
Demand, totalling 55 million kuna, was not met in full, with only 50 million kuna on offer and some lenders and buyers unable to agree terms.
Daily settlements totalled 44.7 million kuna, of which 29.2 million were fresh deals.
Most of the loans were call money, with a rate varied around 10.5 percent, and short term funds granted at 11 percent.
Insurers rolled over previous loans at nine percent and banks charged 10.5 and 12 percent for old one-week borrowings, and 15-16 percent for one-month deals.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Saturday and Monday firmer at 6.0751 to the dollar and 3.5713 to the German mark. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
